title: Regular morphisms remain regular after formal completion
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism between Noetherian quasi-excellent schemes over $\mathbf Q$ [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-exc-excellent-ring]: regular means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] with geometrically regular fibres: for every point $x\in X$ and every finite extension $k'$ of $\kappa(x)$, the base change $Y_x\times_{\kappa(x)}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ of the fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and $J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be coherent ideals [pqf-def-coherent] such that $I\mathcal O_Y\subseteq J$. Write $\widehat X_I$ and $\widehat Y_J$ for the adic formal completions with rings $\varprojlim_n B/I^n$ on affine charts [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. A Noetherian scheme means one with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. A Noetherian adic formal scheme is a ringed space admitting a finite open cover by spaces of the form $\operatorname{Spf}B$, the space of open prime ideals of a Noetherian ring $B$ complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal, with its completed structure sheaf. Such a formal scheme is reduced when its affine chart rings are reduced. Quasi-excellence means quasi-excellence of its affine chart rings [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then the induced formal morphism $\widehat f:\widehat Y_J\to\widehat X_I$ is regular. More explicitly, for formal affine opens $\operatorname{Spf}A\subseteq\widehat X_I$ and $\operatorname{Spf}B\subseteq\widehat Y_J$ with the latter mapping into the former, the ring homomorphism $A\to B$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: flat, with every fibre ring Noetherian and geometrically regular over its residue field (regular after every finite extension of that field). No finite-type condition on $f$ is required.

proof.text: Choose affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$ covering $X$ and $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $A\to B$ is flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its fibre $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and its finite residue-field extensions, are the coordinate rings of the corresponding affine open fibres of $f$. These rings are regular by the hypothesis and the affine regularity convention in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Thus $A\to B$ is regular. Put $C=\widehat A_I$ and $D=\widehat B_J$. By [lem-per-quasi-excellent-formal-affines], these completions and every affine formal open in them have Noetherian quasi-excellent rings. They cover $\widehat X_I$ and $\widehat Y_J$. All ideals here are the restrictions of the given coherent ideals, so their generators are finite.

Since $B$ is quasi-excellent, it is a G-ring by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Thus $B\to D$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular]. Compose with the regular map $A\to B$ using [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition]. Its Noetherian-fibre hypothesis holds: for a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $D\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a localization of the quotient $D/\mathfrak pD$, hence Noetherian because $D$ is Noetherian. Consequently $A\to D$ is regular.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.5, sentence A to B to completed B is regular

proof.text: The containment $IB\subseteq J$ gives compatible maps $A/I^n\to B/J^n$. Passing to compatible sequences defines $u:C\to D$ and gives the commuting triangle $A\to C\to D=A\to B\to D$. Reduction modulo $J$ shows $u(IC)D\subseteq JD$. The ring $D$ is complete for $JD$ by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. Apply [lem-per-completed-base-regularity] with base $A$, ideal $I$, target $D$ and ideal of definition $JD$. Step 2 supplies regularity of $A\to D$, so $C\to D$ is regular. The maps glue since their restrictions are the same maps of compatible sequences. Thus the completed morphism has regular ring maps on the chosen covering pairs.

Check stability under principal refinement. Let $v:C\to D$ be one of the regular chart maps and suppose the formal principal $t$-open maps into the formal principal $s$-open. Replace $t$ by $tv(s)$: its formal principal open is unchanged, because every open prime avoiding $t$ already avoids $v(s)$. Thus, with this replacement, $C_s\to D_t$ exists as an ordinary localization map. The maps $D\to D_t$ and $D_t\to D_{\{t\}}$ are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular] and [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular]. To verify the latter hypothesis, $D_t=D[T]/(tT-1)$ is finite type over $D$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] makes it a G-ring. It is J-2 because every finite type $D_t$-algebra is finite type over $D$ (combine their finite lists of generators), and [def-exc-excellent-ring] supplies openness of its regular locus. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The same argument makes $C_s$ quasi-excellent. Composition and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-through-localization] give regularity of $C_s\to D_{\{t\}}$; now [lem-per-completed-base-regularity] gives regularity of $C_{\{s\}}\to D_{\{t\}}$. Extended original ideals still satisfy containment, and $D_{\{t\}}$ is complete for $JD_{\{t\}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]; final rings are Noetherian, so the composition fibre condition holds as in Step 2 by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The section identifications in [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement] show this is exactly the formal restriction, including the replacement of $t$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.6 first paragraph, with Corollary 2.4.5 expanded into its ring argument

proof.text: Let $\operatorname{Spf}E$ and $\operatorname{Spf}F$ now be arbitrary affine formal opens with the source mapping into the target. They have Noetherian quasi-excellent rings by Step 1. At each source point $y$, choose a covering pair $\operatorname{Spf}C,\operatorname{Spf}D$ from Step 3 containing its image and $y$. By [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement] choose a neighbourhood of the image principal in both $\operatorname{Spf}E$ and $\operatorname{Spf}C$, then a neighbourhood of $y$ principal in both $\operatorname{Spf}F$ and $\operatorname{Spf}D$ and contained in its inverse image. Step 4 proves regularity between these smaller chart rings, say $E_{\{a\}}\to F_{\{b\}}$. The map $E\to E_{\{a\}}$ is a localization followed by completion of a quasi-excellent localization, so the G-ring and J-2 argument of Step 4, followed by localization/completion/composition, gives its regularity. Therefore $E\to F_{\{b\}}$ is regular; the fibre condition of each composition holds as in Step 2 by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], all rings being Noetherian. These principal source opens cover $\operatorname{Spf}F$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.6, reduction to formal principal refinements

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset F$. By [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement] it is a point of $\operatorname{Spf}F$, so one of the Step-5 principal opens contains it, with $b\notin\mathfrak m$. That node supplies a prime $\mathfrak n\subset F_{\{b\}}$ over $\mathfrak m$ and a faithfully flat map $F_{\mathfrak m}\to(F_{\{b\}})_{\mathfrak n}$. Set $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m\cap E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] to the regular map $E\to F_{\{b\}}$ to obtain regularity of $E_{\mathfrak p}\to(F_{\{b\}})_{\mathfrak n}$. Descent [lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence] applied to $E_{\mathfrak p}\to F_{\mathfrak m}\to(F_{\{b\}})_{\mathfrak n}$ gives regularity of $E_{\mathfrak p}\to F_{\mathfrak m}$. As $\mathfrak m$ was arbitrary, the maximal-ideal criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] gives regularity of $E\to F$. This proves the requested assertion on every affine formal chart. Nothing in the argument assumed finite type of $f$.
